summary: An LTP subscription goes to Arrow as ltpc: the 17-byte ltpc packet and a 13-byte ltp packet each become an LTP frame stamped on receipt; after the unsubscribe a packet still in flight reaches nobody.

notes: The query carries appID and token, no login frame (arrow_websocket.py::_build_url).
Neither packet carries a trade or feed time: both sides stamp the receipt time as timestamp and ltt.

deviations.reason: Market-state rule (lead 2026-11-09: the previous close overlays in the snapshot). A 13-byte LTP packet carries no previous close. The bridge keeps the instrument's last known close within one connection (feed/bridge/snapshot.rs, audit C03) and works the change out again from the new price, so the frame carries the close and change the 17-byte packet brought; the web's frame from a 13-byte packet has none (the Arrow adapter keeps no snapshot). Nothing is invented: every value is the broker's.
deviations.ref: feed/bridge/snapshot.rs merge; arrow_websocket.py:556-568 (only the 17-byte packet has a close)
